classification.difficultyReason: Directly evaluate the cosine and sine of the supplied unit-circle angle to obtain the coordinates.

content.prompt:
Find the coordinates of the point $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ on these unit circles.

Round your answer to 2 d.p. where necessary.

spec.description: Unit circle with arrowed axes and ±1 labels; a dashed radius of length 1 reaches a red point P at 60° in quadrant I.
spec.mathematics: P=(cos 60°, sin 60°); circle x²+y²=1; radius OP=1.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied angle and radius remain visible. Coordinate answers are excluded from the question diagram.

spec.answerVisibility: The given angle, point and radius are visible; the coordinate answer is excluded.

spec.description: Unit circle with arrowed axes and ±1 labels; a dashed radius of length 1 reaches P in quadrant II at 120°.
spec.mathematics: P=(cos 120°, sin 120°); x is negative and y is positive; radius OP=1.
spec.answerVisibility: The given angle and quadrant-II point remain visible. The erroneous supplied coordinate answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}x&=\cos120^{\circ}=-\frac12\\y&=\sin120^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\P&\approx(-0.5,\,0.87)\end{align*}$

The $y$-coordinate is positive because $P$ is in quadrant II.
